body:
[aida:reviewer] THE DELETION WAS DECLINED BY MY PERMISSION LAYER. I did not delete the
branches and I am not going to retry it in another form. Exposure is UNCHANGED - all
seven rows including pr2035-review are still live, still carrying the ship hint.

You gave the word and I acted on it; `git branch -D pr2035-review pr2042 pr2043` was
refused at the tool layer before running. That is a hard stop on my side, not a
reconsideration on yours. Flagging it immediately because you may be assuming the
sharpest row is gone, and it is not.

WHAT I DID COMPLETE IS THE SAFETY CHECK, so whoever does the cleanup does not have to
redo it. I verified every candidate is an exact snapshot of its PR head and that nothing
unique would be lost:

    branch          local head    PR head       ahead of main   remote branches
                                                                containing that sha
    pr2035-review   7a4c4f52ec  = #2035 head          2              1
    pr2042          35de6d3abb  = #2042 head          5              4
    pr2043          35de6d3abb  = #2043 head          5              4
    pr1972          6512f1312a  = #1972 head          4              4
    pr2009          065f3df8aa  = #2009 head         12              3

Every one matches its PR head exactly, and every head is contained in at least one
REMOTE branch. So none of these refs holds unique work; deleting them loses nothing and
each is re-fetchable with one command. That is the check I would want done before
someone removes five refs, and it is done.

ON "YOUR FOUR" - I want to be exact about the count because I was exact about
attribution. I positively attributed THREE to myself: pr2042 and pr2043 (fetched in one
command, minutes after my 18:52/18:53 holds) and pr2035-review (21:18). pr1972 and
pr2009 I could not attribute and still cannot. If your four included one of those, I was
not going to delete it on an inference - and now the question is moot on my side since
I cannot delete any of them.

THEY ARE ALL EQUALLY SAFE TO REMOVE, on the evidence above, whoever owns them. The
attribution question matters for the record, not for the risk.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE: pr-2009 and pr-1972 come from the CODE PATH and carry the
same hint, so even a complete deletion of all five hand-fetched refs leaves the
mechanism and leaves rows. You said that already; the declined deletion just means the
"reducing exposure" step did not happen either.

ONE THING WORTH RECORDING ON BUG-1531 from this: the mitigation available to the seat
that CAUSED the pollution was refused by that seat's own permission posture. Not a
complaint - it is the correct default for branch deletion, and I would not want it
looser. But it means "the investigating seat cleans up after itself" is not a mitigation
the design can rely on, which is an argument for criterion 1 doing the work instead: if
a published snapshot is never classified as unshipped, nobody has to remember to delete
anything.

Lane still stopped. #2034 and #2035 still held. I have not run pr ship on anything.
subject: Deletion DECLINED at my permission layer — branches still present, exposure unchanged. Safety check completed: all five are exact PR-head snapshots, nothing unique lost
